record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README uses a difference-in-means refusal direction for token attribution and trigger rewriting, but reports no ablation or addition of that direction to test causal mediation.
record.gate_note: Probe AUCs, output-logit prediction, and trigger attribution are reported results, but do not establish that ablating or adding the direction causes refusal changes. The behavior-flipping summary does not specify which behaviors flipped.
record.test_reason: The README uses a difference-in-means refusal direction only as a tool, projecting token hidden states onto it to find trigger tokens to rewrite. It never ablates or adds the direction and reports no refusal rate under such an intervention. Its reported results are probe AUCs, output-logit prediction, unembedding readouts, and prompt-rewriting flip rates. None of these bear on whether the direction mediates refusal or on any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. More fully, the authors conclude that refusal is linearly decodable and fully formed before generation. They also claim it peaks at 67% depth in Gemma and 87% in Qwen, and that the direction reads as multilingual hedging. They say refusal is triggered by request specificity rather than harm keywords. No causal mediation claim is made.
record.recipe_differences: Tool-style hackathon repository: uses residual-stream probes and difference-in-means direction attribution, but reports no projection ablation or direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported best refusal-probe layers differ by model: L40 (67% depth) for Gemma and L56 (87% depth) for Qwen; last-token pooling is reported for both.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes classify refusal at AUC 0.955 (Gemma, L40) and 0.866 (Qwen, L56), and beat MLP and attention probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal is linearly decodable from residual-stream activations at mid-to-late layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Output logits on five first tokens predict refusal with AUC 0.930.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal decision is readable from first-token logits before generation.

fits_no_version.finding: Projected through the unembedding, the diff-in-means direction's top tokens are 'although' in several languages. Gemma's direction loads on specificity tokens, Qwen's on chat-template tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction's vocabulary readout is a cross-lingual hedging concept, and its token loading differs across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Rewriting attribution-identified trigger regions flips the probe 100% and behavior 60% on n=20 Gemma examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rewriting prompts guided by refusal-direction attribution can flip refusal behavior.

record.problems: README-only results; code and experiments were not read or run. The README does not state uncertainty estimates or null controls, and does not give enough detail to determine what the Level 2 behavior flips represent. No general-capability evaluation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the difference-in-means direction, no refusal rate after intervention, no capability check.
Rewriting is guided by direction attribution, but the study does not show that this suppresses the direction or that attacks work through it. No adversarial training.
No comparison of one direction against several. The claim that the 'boundary is genuinely linear' rests only on probe comparisons.
No separation of harm judgment from the refusal decision. The 'specificity not harm keywords' finding is attribution-based only.
Directions are computed separately per model and only described qualitatively. No transfer test. The multilingual unembedding tokens are not a cross-language intervention.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
Qwen 3.6 has <think> tokens, but there is no causal test of the direction in reasoning.

record.verdict_notes: This is a hackathon README only; the code was not read. There are no controls or uncertainty estimates, and the Level 2 sample is n=20. Because the study only uses the direction for attribution, it is T4 with no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No causal ablation or addition of the direction, refusal rate after intervention, or general-capability check.
No weight edit or released-model refusal evaluation.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer evaluation.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
No test of causal direction ablation or addition in reasoning models.
